sections.title: Appearance
lines: A much larger version of an ordinary frog, with camouflaging coloration. It ranges from two to six feet long and 50 to 250 pounds. At two feet it weighs 50 pounds, increasing by 50 pounds for each additional foot.

sections.title: Hit Dice variants mechanics
lines: 1 HD · 2 feet long. THAC0 19, bite 1–3, 120 XP.
2 HD · The text gives 2 to 4 feet. THAC0 16, bite 1–6, 175 XP. The 2-foot endpoint overlaps the 1 HD description.
3 HD · Over 4 feet long. THAC0 16, bite 2–8, 270 XP.

sections.title: Movement and ambush mechanics
lines: Jump · A 50-pound frog can leap up to 180 feet. Subtract 20 feet per additional 50 pounds. It can leap 30 feet straight up. It cannot leap backward or directly sideways.
Camouflage · In its natural habitat, opponents take −3 to surprise rolls. It retreats from fire.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Tongue · Its sticky tongue reaches three times its body length and gains a +4 bonus to the attack roll. A hit causes no direct damage. The target gets one chance to strike the tongue before being reeled in. A hit frees the target, and the frog leaves that target alone.

Reeling in prey · A lighter victim is drawn in during the round they miss the tongue. A heavier victim takes one extra round and gets another chance to hit the tongue. A victim more than twice the frog’s weight cannot be drawn in and is released on the third round after capture. The text leaves equal weight unspecified.
First bite · A successful bite in the first round the victim is in reach deals the maximum damage for the frog’s Hit Dice.

Swallow whole · An attack roll of 20 can swallow a victim shorter than 3 feet. A victim has three rounds to escape before asphyxiating. An attack roll of 18 or higher with an edged weapon lets the victim cut their way out. A successful escape kills the frog. Damage dealt to the frog has a 33% chance to also affect the swallowed victim.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: 5–40 appearing. Uncommon. Pack organization. Active at any time. Carnivore. No intelligence (0).
Average (8) morale. Treasure, alignment, and magic resistance Nil.
The printed Hit Dice cell reads 1+3. The prose describes 1, 2, and 3 HD versions, which also appear in the THAC0 and XP rows. The profile uses those versions.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, p. 119.

lines: Amphibious. The frog can breathe air and water. Standing Leap. The frog’s long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start.

sections.title: Actions
lines: Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the frog can’t bite another target. Swallow. The frog makes one bite attack against a Small or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is swallowed, and the grapple ends. The swallowed target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the frog, and it takes 5 (2d4) acid damage at the start of each of the frog’s turns. The frog can have only one target swallowed at a time. If the frog dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting prone.

lines: Bite. Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 11). Swallow. The frog swallows a Small or smaller target it is grappling. While swallowed, the target isn’t Grappled but has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, and it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the frog. At the end of the frog’s next turn, the swallowed target takes 5 (2d4) Acid damage. If that damage doesn’t kill it, the frog disgorges it, causing it to exit Prone.
